findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed burger holder to be hot holding at 110F. Discussed with PIC, warmer was turned to a hotter setting and tested at 155F. Ensure any TCS item is being hot held at at least 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness.
findings.comment: Observed PIC to be wearing a sleeveless shirt. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and sleeveless shirts will no longer be used. Ensure proper clothing is worn in kitchen to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-304.11 Clean Condition. Food employees shall wear clean outer clothing to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the water/tea bar soda gun to be soiled with black mold. Discussed with PIC, soda gun will be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soda guns are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed kitchen prep cooler to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, prep cooler will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevent food debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: Observed the hot dog cooker to not have any overhead cover. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all food cooking has proper overhead protection. 
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.comment:

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications.

4-202.16: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.comment:

findings.comment:

Inspector moved the ice scoop. Discussed with PIC/CFPM. Ensure staff is aware the bar hand sink must be left open and available for staff to properly wash hands. Ice scoop should be placed away from the hand sink. COS.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-101.11: (A) PERMIT HOLDER shall be PIC or shall designate PIC and ensure the PIC is present during all hours of operation. (B) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT with multiple departments on same PREMISES can designate single PIC when food is not being prepared. 

(REPEAT) Observed no person-in-charge (PIC) to be a certified food protection manager (CFPM). There is a general lack of managerial oversight. The facility needs 2 CFPM’s present for operational hours and both should know basics in food safety and service, as well as how to provide necessary answers/documentation for a routine food inspection. Food handling staff had limited knowledge in sanitizing process, hand washing, date marking, test strip use. All documentation (licenses, employee health reporting agreements, Norovirus illness clean-up policy, etc.) is not available. There must be a CFPM’s presence and more oversight for the facility. Education was provided to the employee working who was a food handler. Education must be conducted with staff. Inspector will follow-up on 7/11/23 (Inspector has a scheduled vacation and will not be available within 10-day follow-up window).

Repeat since last routine inspection on 5/11/22.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed no certified food protection manager present during inspection. Facility needs at least one CFPM present during all operational hours. Facility likely needs 2 total. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last two routine inspections.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements available. Provided copy. Ensure all new hires and employees read and sign document. Create a public health binder for these documents. Provided new copy for facility. Inspector will follow-up on 7/11/23 (Inspector has a scheduled vacation and will not be available within 10-day follow-up window).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy available for the facility. Discussed with PIC. Provided new copy. Facility should have bleach to perform procedure. Hang on the bulletin boards in the kitchen. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed the food handler to improperly wash hands - no barrier was used to turn off the faucets after hand washing. Discussed with PIC. Ensure proper hand washing protocols are reviewed with staff. Barrier such as a paper towel should be used to turn off faucets after washing hands. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

(REPEAT) Observed no soap at the bar hand sink. Discussed with employee. Employee brought soap to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly stocked at all times. Repeat from last routine inspection on 5/11/22.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

(REPEAT) Observed the bar hand sink to be blocked by a large ice scoop and a spatula. Cease practice. Ensure hand sinks are open and available at all times for employees to wash hands. Items were moved. Education was provided. Repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/11/22.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact surfaces to be dirty:
1. Drip pan within the hot holding unit (with burgers, hot dogs) has a layer of old drip splash that is moldy. The drip pan needs washed, rinsed, and sanitized routinely in order to prevent contamination. 
2. The ice machine in the back has a layer of pink/black mold along the interior baffle of the ice machine. Pink mold is visible on the baffle lip with a flash light is shined into the ice machine. The ice machine needs washed, rinsed, and sanitized routinely to prevent mold build-up. Inspector instructed facility to remove all ice and wash, rinse, sanitize the interior of the ice machine. 

Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean these areas. Inspector will follow-up on 7/11/23 (Inspector has a scheduled vacation and will not be available within 10-day follow-up window).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed multiple bags of hot dogs within the back reach-in cooler labeled, “KEGS ONLY”, to be 48F probed. The cooler is likely operating out of temperature and only alcohol should be stored in this cooler as the front sign states. Hot dogs were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff is aware not to put foods in this cooler. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed the brats and hot dogs within the bottom refrigerator in the kitchen to lack a date. Discussed with worker. Worker provided date marking for the items. Ensure items that are pulled from the freezer and defrosted have date marking provided. A 7-day date marking rule should be utilized. Education with staff is needed. Ensure the CFPM explains this process to all staff. COS.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-301.11: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be separated from one another for RETAIL sale. (B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be located in area not above FOOD or FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. 

Observed bottle of mosquito repellent and perfume to be on a shelving unit in the kitchen that is above blenders and other clean food-contact surfaces. Cease practice. Ensure staff is aware not to place toxic materials above food-contact surfaces. Items should be on the bottom shelf or away from food areas. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. 

Observed no probe style thermometer for the facility. Discussed with PIC. Ensure facility purchased or obtains a probe style thermometer. Inspector will follow-up on 7/11/23 (Inspector has a scheduled vacation and will not be available within 10-day follow-up window).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed several coolers to be missing hanging thermometers within coolers. Ensure all cold holding units have hanging thermometers. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Observed multiple in-use rags on the bar counter and kitchen counters. Discussed with PIC. Ensure staff is aware rags need to be immersed in sanitizer when not in use. Sanitizer should be the appropriate concentration. Rags should not just be lying on the counters wet. Ensure staff is aware to make sani buckets and keep rags within them when not being used. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no active sani bucket at the start of the inspection. When prompting employee, employee provided a general cleaning spray as the substance the facility uses to sanitize surfaces. Cease practice. Quaternary ammonium and/or bleach should be used to sanitize surfaces. Create sani buckets for the in-use rags (see violation #41) and/or spray bottle with paper towels (label spray bottle with common name of substance in black marker - ex: “bleach”). Education needs to be provided to all staff. There is limited sanitizing knowledge at the facility based on today’s inspection. Inspector will follow-up on 7/11/23 (Inspector has a scheduled vacation and will not be available within 10-day follow-up window).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Observed no quaternary ammonium test strips for the bar. Bar is using this product for the 3 compartment sink. Discussed with PIC. Ensure test strips are available and being used to monitor sanitization concentrations. Inspector will follow-up on 7/11/23 (Inspector has a scheduled vacation and will not be available within 10-day follow-up window).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-301.12: (A) Sink with 3-compartments shall be provided for EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS. (B) Sinks shall be capable of accommodating the immersion of the largest piece of EQUIPMENT or UTENSIL. A machine or alternative option can be used. Reference 4-301.12 Pf (C) Alternative manual WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may be used for special cleaning C

Observed the back kitchen hand sink that is capable of wash, rinsing, and sanitizing to be totally blocked by mechanical equipment in front of the sink and within all 3 basins. Facility is not utilizing the 3 compartment sink. When prompted, employee stated they use a single sink in the kitchen to wash dishes. Cease practice. This is incorrect. When asked if the bar 3 compartment sink is used for washing tongs, knives, etc., the employee stated no. The back 3 compartment sink needs to be operational again and used. 

The bar 3 compartment sink only had the first two basins contained with soapy water and quaternary ammonium. The, “rinse”, step is being missed - WASH, RINSE, SANITIZE to reflect the 3 basins. Provided education for the employee. 

Inspector will follow-up on 7/11/23 (Inspector has a scheduled vacation and will not be available within 10-day follow-up window).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-501.16: (A) WAREWASHING sink may not be used for handwashing. (B) If WAREWASHING sink used to wash wiping cloths, wash produce, or thaw food, it shall be cleaned before and after each time. 

Observed a paper towel dispenser and paper towels by the back 3 compartment sink indicating hand washing use. Cease practice. Items need to be removed from the 3 compartment sink. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Drywall observed to be damaged in several locations (women’s bathroom by hand sinks and 3 compartment sink in the back). Areas have brown paper exposed - walls must be smooth and easily cleanable. Drywall at 3 compartment sink is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/11/22.
2. Hand sink in the kitchen needs re-caulked to the wall (coming away from sink and wall).
3. The flooring in front of the ice machine in the back is missing. A black rug is covering the exposed particle board. Replace the tile.
4. Under the 3 compartment sink at the bar: the wall is just particle board - needs painted/sealed to be smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent. Coving is missing in this area as well - apply coving so wall and floor meet smoothly.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed only a limited number of food handler’s licenses. Ensure all staff has a food handler’s license and copies are left at the facility. License is valid for 3 years. Ensure new hired obtain license within 30 days of employment. Correct by next routine inspection.

Soap is provided at 3-compartment sink and food prep sink. Remove soap/paper towels and only use sink for 3- compartment sink for dishwashing; only use food prep sink for food prep. CORRECTED- Removed soap from non-handwashing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.13 A sink used for FOOD preparation or UTENSIL washing, or a service sink or curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water or similar wastes, may not be provided with the handwashing aids and devices required for a HANDWASHING SINK as specified under §§ 6-301.11 and 6-301.12 and ¶ 5-501.16(C). (C)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Ice machine is soiled with brown build-up and is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Working container of blue liquid not properly labeled. CORRECTED- Person in charge labeled the container. 
7-102.11 Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. (Pf)

Soap and Sani-Tabs are stored above single service items.  CORRECTED- Employee moved materials to separated storage. 
7-201.11 POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be stored so they can not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES by (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning. (P)

Cl sanitizer concentration is over 200ppm (bleached out test strip), exceeding the maximum toxic level for use on a food-contact surface, as specified by manufacturer. CORRECTED- Sanitizer was diluted to a concentration of 200ppm.
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940
Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface
sanitizing solutions). (P)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Provide test strips for both Cl and quat since both are used in the kitchen.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. (Pf)

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a blue liquid in spray bottle with no label. Properly label containers with name of chemical. Corrected. Bottle labeled correctly. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
